title: Weak Serre and coproduct closure of integral ind-constructible modules
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite intermediate extension in the fixed algebraic closure [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $k$ a field of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for the continuous condensed ring of integers, $\Lambda_X$ for its pullback to $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, and $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$ for its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $H_X$ be the finite constant-model constructible predicate and $B_X$ the bounded constructible predicate in $D(\mathcal A_X)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Define $\operatorname{IndCons}_X=H_X.\mathrm{ind}$ using small filtered diagrams in the hom universe, and $\operatorname{Dic}_X=\{K\mid \forall n\in\mathbf Z,\ H^n(K)\in\operatorname{IndCons}_X\}$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Then $\operatorname{IndCons}_X$ contains zero, is closed under ambient kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects and under extensions, and is closed under every ambient coproduct indexed in the hom universe, including the empty coproduct.

proof.text: Use integral constant-model constructible closure for kernels, cokernels and extensions. The zero scalar module on the identity cover and one-stratum stratification gives a constructible zero. Finite type over k makes X Noetherian.

Apply integral Ext/Hom continuity to degree-zero inputs, using the fully faithful single functor and the zero shift to deduce finite presentability of each constructible module. Essential smallness of finite stratified models and the canonical filtered presentation then give the common presentation of arrows. Apply the coefficient-independent kernel/cokernel argument to those presentations and exact ambient filtered colimits. For extensions, use integral degree-one continuity and the general finitely-presentable extension descent argument: descend the extension class to a constructible kernel stage, push out, and take the filtered colimit.

Finite sums are constructible by split extensions. An arbitrary sum is the filtered colimit of its finite partial sums. Flatten the filtered constructible presentations using finite tuples of presentation stages. Its cocones are exactly families of maps from the original summands. The zero model handles the empty family.

lean.statement:
theorem integralIndConstructibleHeartClosure
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p₀ : ℕ) [CharP k p₀] (hp₀ : 0 < p₀) (hpℓ : p₀ ≠ ℓ)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] :
    let Λ := Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E
    let A := Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)
    let P := ObjectProperty.ind.{u + 1} (IsConstantModelConstructible Λ X)
    P.ContainsZero ∧ P.IsClosedUnderKernels ∧ P.IsClosedUnderCokernels ∧
      P.IsClosedUnderExtensions ∧
      (∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) (M : I → A) (c : Cofan M), IsColimit c →
        (∀ i, P (M i)) → P c.pt)
